styleSelection.reason: Requested loose ink and wash. The lit meadows and tan paths are flat light planes: one connected full-strength wash each, a shadow glaze only where trees cast shade, and the pen carries their edges. Sepia pen sketch first, selective closing ink last.

HILLS.woods.reason: The oak woods are the dark mass that the meadows cut through. They need three value steps the two-band ink-and-wash ladder lacks: a pale teal-grey base, mid crown bodies on dry paper, then blue-black shadow glazes under the crowns and in the ravine. Separate from the meadows, so their washes never average with the meadow colour.

families.referenceCue: lit acid yellow-green grass slopes on diagonals and the tan dirt paths; the lower meadow is the anchor box, so the bright meadow, light meadow and khaki path colour clusters label as meadow wherever they lie

dense oak woodland: rounded crowns, lit grey-green tops, teal bodies, blue-black undersides and ravine shadow; the grey-green, teal and dark colour clusters label as woods, so the woods mid layers and glazes run as one connected mass without paper specks
